This notebook walks through the format with **standard libraries only**. It
loads neither sceptre nor pysceptre. Every step is shown in R and in Python:
choose a language in any tab set and every tab set on the page follows.

The files it reads are the committed ones in `example/` and `conformance/`.
The code that does the reading and writing is the prototype in `format/`
(`sceptre_format.R`, `sceptre_format.py`), which is temporary: it moves into
the packages when they adopt the format. What it writes goes to
`verify/out/notebook/`, which is not committed.

R and Python run in **one process** here (knitr, with reticulate for Python),
each with its own copy of the HDF5 library. That was tested on macOS only and
is not known to work on Linux. One constraint holds on any platform: a
language cannot write a file the other still holds open, so each side closes
its handles before the other writes.

```{r}
#| label: setup-r
#| include: false
source("format/setup.R")
library(reticulate)
out <- "verify/out/notebook"
unlink(out, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(out, recursive = TRUE)
options(width = 110)
```

```{python}
#| label: setup-python
#| include: false
import json
import shutil
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import h5py
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

sys.path.insert(0, "format")
import sceptre_format as sf

pd.set_option("display.width", 110)
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 12)
pd.set_option("display.max_colwidth", 90)
out = Path("verify/out/notebook")
```

## 1. What is on disk

A dataset is one data file, `screen.h5mu`. An analysis of it is one folder,
with a folder per stage and a cache of fitted models. Any number of analyses
can sit beside one data file.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## R

```{r}
file_listing("example/highmoi/analyses/left_sided")
```

The data file is a MuData file: one group per modality under `mod/`.

```{r}
layout <- rhdf5::h5ls("example/highmoi/screen.h5mu", recursive = 3)
layout[layout$group %in% c("/", "/mod", "/mod/rna", "/mod/grna", "/uns"), c("group", "name", "otype")]
```

## Python

```{python}
sf.file_listing("example/highmoi/analyses/left_sided")
```

The data file is a MuData file: one group per modality under `mod/`.

```{python}
with h5py.File("example/highmoi/screen.h5mu") as f:
    for group in ("/", "mod", "mod/rna", "mod/grna", "uns"):
        print(f"{group:10}", ", ".join(f[group].keys()))
```

:::

## 2. Reading the data file

R reads it as a `SingleCellExperiment` with the gRNA counts as an alternative
experiment. Python reads it as a `MuData` object. Both are the standard
containers of their language.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## R

```{r}
sce <- fmt_read_screen("example/highmoi/screen.h5mu")
rhdf5::h5closeAll()   # MuData's reader leaves a handle open
sce
```

Cell covariates, with each modality's measurements under its name:

```{r}
head(as.data.frame(colData(sce)), 3)
```

The gRNA table and the file's metadata:

```{r}
head(as.data.frame(rowData(altExp(sce, "gRNA"))), 3)
str(S4Vectors::metadata(sce)$sceptre)
```

## Python

```{python}
mdata = sf.read_screen("example/highmoi/screen.h5mu")
mdata
```

Cell covariates, with each modality's measurements under its name:

```{python}
sf.covariate_table(mdata).head(3)
```

The gRNA table and the file's metadata:

```{python}
print(mdata["grna"].var.head(3))
mdata.uns["sceptre"]
```

:::

## 3. Reading an analysis

An analysis folder has one `record.json` per stage, written last, which lists
the stage's tables with their row counts. The tables are Parquet files.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## R

```{r}
saved <- fmt_read_analysis("example/highmoi/analyses/left_sided")
names(saved$stages)
data.frame(table = names(saved$tables), rows = vapply(saved$tables, nrow, integer(1)), row.names = NULL)
```

The settings of the parameters stage, and the first discovery results:

```{r}
str(saved$stages$parameters$settings)
head(saved$tables[["discovery/results"]], 3)
```

## Python

```{python}
saved = sf.read_analysis("example/highmoi/analyses/left_sided")
print(list(saved["stages"]))
pd.DataFrame({"table": list(saved["tables"]), "rows": [len(t) for t in saved["tables"].values()]})
```

The settings of the parameters stage, and the first discovery results:

```{python}
print(json.dumps(saved["stages"]["parameters"]["settings"], indent=1))
saved["tables"]["discovery/results"].head(3)
```

:::

## 4. What the files imply

The format stores each fact once. A reader computes the rest: which cells
carry each target, the groups of control gRNAs, which results are
significant, and the log2 fold change. Each is compared here with what
sceptre itself held, captured once in `example/highmoi/expected/`.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## R

```{r}
expected <- read_json("example/highmoi/expected/left_sided/expected.json")
tables <- saved$tables
cells <- colnames(sce)
grna <- altExp(sce, "gRNA")
strategy <- saved$stages$parameters$settings$grna_integration_strategy
grna_table <- data.frame(grna_id = rownames(grna), as.data.frame(rowData(grna)), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
grna_table$grna_group <- grna_groups(grna_table, strategy)

# cells of each gRNA, from the assignments table, pooled by target
by_grna <- cells_by_grna(tables[["assignment/assignments"]], rownames(grna), cells)
pooled <- group_cells(by_grna, grna_table)
head(lengths(pooled$grna_group_idxs), 4)

# the cells in use after QC
kept <- tables[["qc/cells"]]
in_use <- kept$in_use[match(cells, kept$cell_id)]
c(cells = length(cells), in_use = sum(in_use), same_as_sceptre = identical(sha256_ids(cells[in_use]), expected$cells_in_use_sha256))

# significance comes from the threshold the stage recorded; log2 fold change from the fold change
results <- add_significant(add_log_2_fold_change(tables[["discovery/results"]]), saved$stages$discovery$significance_threshold)
want <- read_table("example/highmoi/expected/left_sided/discovery.parquet")
both <- merge(want, results, by = unit_key(want), suffixes = c("_expected", ""))
derived <- c(pairs = nrow(both), significant = sum(both$significant, na.rm = TRUE),
  significant_same_as_sceptre = identical(both$significant, both$significant_expected),
  log2_same_as_sceptre = isTRUE(all.equal(both$log_2_fold_change, both$log_2_fold_change_expected, tolerance = 1e-12)))
stopifnot(derived[3:4] == 1, identical(sha256_ids(cells[in_use]), expected$cells_in_use_sha256))   # the render stops if a comparison fails
derived
```

## Python

```{python}
expected = json.loads(Path("example/highmoi/expected/left_sided/expected.json").read_text())
tables = saved["tables"]
cells = np.asarray(mdata["grna"].obs_names, dtype=object)
strategy = saved["stages"]["parameters"]["settings"]["grna_integration_strategy"]
grna_table = mdata["grna"].var.reset_index(names="grna_id")
grna_table["grna_group"] = sf.grna_groups(grna_table, strategy)

# cells of each gRNA, from the assignments table, pooled by target
by_grna = sf.cells_by_grna(tables["assignment/assignments"], list(mdata["grna"].var_names), pd.Index(cells))
by_group, by_control = sf.group_cells(by_grna, grna_table)
print({name: len(idx) for name, idx in list(by_group.items())[:4]})

# the cells in use after QC
in_use = tables["qc/cells"].set_index("cell_id").loc[cells, "in_use"].to_numpy(dtype=bool)
print({"cells": len(cells), "in_use": int(in_use.sum()), "same_as_sceptre": sf.sha256_ids(cells[in_use]) == expected["cells_in_use_sha256"]})

# significance comes from the threshold the stage recorded; log2 fold change from the fold change
results = sf.add_significant(sf.add_log_2_fold_change(tables["discovery/results"]), saved["stages"]["discovery"].get("significance_threshold"))
want = sf.read_table("example/highmoi/expected/left_sided/discovery.parquet")
both = want.merge(results, on=sf.unit_key(want), suffixes=("_expected", ""))
derived = {"pairs": len(both), "significant": int(both["significant"].sum()),
 "significant_same_as_sceptre": bool((both["significant"] == both["significant_expected"]).all()),
 "log2_same_as_sceptre": bool(np.allclose(both["log_2_fold_change"], both["log_2_fold_change_expected"], rtol=1e-12, equal_nan=True))}
assert derived["significant_same_as_sceptre"] and derived["log2_same_as_sceptre"]   # the render stops if a comparison fails
assert sf.sha256_ids(cells[in_use]) == expected["cells_in_use_sha256"]
derived
```

:::

## 5. One language writes, the other reads

Each language writes its own copy of the data file and of the analysis, from
what it read above.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## R

```{r}
copy_analysis_r <- function(saved, directory) {
    fmt_init_analysis(directory, saved$screen, saved$response_modality)
    for (stage in names(saved$stages)) {
        record <- saved$stages[[stage]]
        listed <- paste0(stage, "/", sub("\\.parquet$", "", vapply(record$files, function(f) f$path, character(1))))
        fmt_write_stage(directory, stage, record[setdiff(names(record), c("stage", "provenance", "files"))], saved$tables[listed], record$provenance)
    }
    fmt_write_fits(directory, saved$tables[[FITS]], saved$fits_identity)
}
fmt_write_screen(sce, file.path(out, "screen-r.h5mu"))
copy_analysis_r(saved, file.path(out, "analysis-r"))
rhdf5::h5closeAll()
list.files(out)
```

## Python

```{python}
def copy_analysis(saved, directory):
    sf.init_analysis(directory, saved["screen"], saved["response_modality"])
    for stage, record in saved["stages"].items():
        listed = [f"{stage}/{f['path'].removesuffix('.parquet')}" for f in record["files"]]
        body = {k: v for k, v in record.items() if k not in ("stage", "provenance", "files")}
        sf.write_stage(directory, stage, body, {name: saved["tables"][name] for name in listed}, record["provenance"])
    sf.write_fits(directory, saved["tables"][sf.FITS], saved["fits_identity"])

sf.write_screen(mdata, out / "screen-python.h5mu")
copy_analysis(saved, out / "analysis-python")
sorted(p.name for p in out.iterdir())
```

:::

Then each reads what the other wrote, and compares it with what it read from
the example.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## R

```{r}
theirs <- fmt_read_screen(file.path(out, "screen-python.h5mu"))
theirs_analysis <- fmt_read_analysis(file.path(out, "analysis-python"))
rhdf5::h5closeAll()
crossed <- c(
    counts = identical(counts(theirs), counts(sce)),
    grna_counts = identical(counts(altExp(theirs, "gRNA")), counts(altExp(sce, "gRNA"))),
    covariates = isTRUE(all.equal(as.data.frame(colData(theirs)), as.data.frame(colData(sce)))),
    tables = all(vapply(names(saved$tables), function(name) same_table(theirs_analysis$tables[[name]], saved$tables[[name]]), logical(1))),
    conforms = nrow(validate_screen(file.path(out, "screen-python.h5mu"))) == 0L &&
        nrow(validate_analysis(file.path(out, "analysis-python"), file.path(out, "screen-python.h5mu"))) == 0L
)
stopifnot(crossed, grepl("^rna_", grep("n_umis", names(colData(theirs)), value = TRUE)[1]))
crossed
```

## Python

```{python}
theirs = sf.read_screen(out / "screen-r.h5mu")
theirs_analysis = sf.read_analysis(out / "analysis-r")
crossed = {
    "counts": (theirs["rna"].X != mdata["rna"].X).nnz == 0,
    "grna_counts": (theirs["grna"].X != mdata["grna"].X).nnz == 0,
    "covariates": sf.covariate_table(theirs).equals(sf.covariate_table(mdata)),
    "tables": all(sf.same_table(theirs_analysis["tables"][name], saved["tables"][name]) for name in saved["tables"]),
    "conforms": len(sf.validate_screen(out / "screen-r.h5mu")) == 0
                and len(sf.validate_analysis(out / "analysis-r", out / "screen-r.h5mu")) == 0,
}
assert all(crossed.values()) and "rna_n_umis" in sf.covariate_table(theirs)
crossed
```

:::

The two data files hold the same arrays in the same number types:

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## R

```{r}
arrays <- as.vector(outer(c("data", "indices", "indptr"), c("rna", "grna"), function(a, m) paste0("mod/", m, "/X/", a)))
same <- vapply(arrays, function(path) identical(
    as.vector(rhdf5::h5read(file.path(out, "screen-r.h5mu"), path)),
    as.vector(rhdf5::h5read(file.path(out, "screen-python.h5mu"), path))), logical(1))
rhdf5::h5closeAll()
listing <- rhdf5::h5ls(file.path(out, "screen-r.h5mu"), all = TRUE)
type <- vapply(arrays, function(path) listing$dtype[paste0(listing$group, "/", listing$name) == paste0("/", path)], character(1))
stopifnot(same)
data.frame(array = arrays, identical = unname(same), type = unname(type))
```

## Python

```{python}
rows = []
with h5py.File(out / "screen-r.h5mu") as a, h5py.File(out / "screen-python.h5mu") as b:
    for modality in ("rna", "grna"):
        for array in ("data", "indices", "indptr"):
            path = f"mod/{modality}/X/{array}"
            rows.append({"array": path, "identical": bool(np.array_equal(a[path][()], b[path][()])),
                         "type_r": str(a[path].dtype), "type_python": str(b[path].dtype)})
assert all(row["identical"] and row["type_r"] == row["type_python"] for row in rows)
pd.DataFrame(rows)
```

:::

## 6. What a reader tolerates, and what it refuses

Writers are strict and readers are lenient. A file whose counts or index
arrays are stored in another number type does not conform, and a reader
still reads it to the same counts (rule S4.4). Other files a reader must
refuse, because reading them would give wrong answers silently.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## R

```{r}
cases <- jsonlite::fromJSON("conformance/cases.json", simplifyVector = FALSE)
tolerated <- Filter(function(case) !is.null(case$reads_as), cases)
do.call(rbind, lapply(tolerated, function(case) {
    a <- fmt_read_screen(case$path)
    b <- fmt_read_screen(case$reads_as)
    rhdf5::h5closeAll()
    data.frame(file = basename(case$path), rules_broken = paste(unlist(case$expect), collapse = ", "), same_counts = identical(counts(a), counts(b)))
}))
```

```{r}
refused <- Filter(function(case) isTRUE(case$reader_refuses), cases)
do.call(rbind, lapply(refused, function(case) {
    message <- tryCatch({
        if (case$kind == "screen") fmt_read_screen(case$path) else fmt_read_analysis(case$path)
        "READ, AND SHOULD NOT HAVE BEEN"
    }, error = function(e) conditionMessage(e))
    rhdf5::h5closeAll()
    data.frame(file = basename(case$path), reader_says = substr(message, 1, 80))
}))
```

## Python

```{python}
cases = json.loads(Path("conformance/cases.json").read_text())
rows = []
for case in cases:
    if "reads_as" in case:
        a, b = sf.read_screen(case["path"]), sf.read_screen(case["reads_as"])
        rows.append({"file": Path(case["path"]).name, "rules_broken": ", ".join(case["expect"]),
                     "same_counts": all((a[m].X != b[m].X).nnz == 0 for m in b.mod)})
pd.DataFrame(rows)
```

```{python}
rows = []
for case in cases:
    if case.get("reader_refuses"):
        try:
            sf.read_screen(case["path"]) if case["kind"] == "screen" else sf.read_analysis(case["path"])
            says = "READ, AND SHOULD NOT HAVE BEEN"
        except ValueError as error:
            says = str(error)
        rows.append({"file": Path(case["path"]).name, "reader_says": says[:80]})
pd.DataFrame(rows)
```

:::

## 7. The validators

`validate_screen()` and `validate_analysis()` check files against the
numbered rules of `SPEC.md` without building any object. They return one row
per problem, and no rows when the files conform.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## R

```{r}
nrow(validate_screen("example/highmoi/screen.h5mu"))
nrow(validate_analysis("example/highmoi/analyses/left_sided", "example/highmoi/screen.h5mu"))
validate_screen("conformance/invalid/screens/stored_zero.h5mu")
validate_analysis("conformance/invalid/analyses/significant_stored", "conformance/valid/highmoi_written_by_r.h5mu")
```

## Python

```{python}
print(len(sf.validate_screen("example/highmoi/screen.h5mu")))
print(len(sf.validate_analysis("example/highmoi/analyses/left_sided", "example/highmoi/screen.h5mu")))
print(sf.validate_screen("conformance/invalid/screens/stored_zero.h5mu").to_string(index=False))
print(sf.validate_analysis("conformance/invalid/analyses/significant_stored", "conformance/valid/highmoi_written_by_r.h5mu").to_string(index=False))
```

:::

## 8. Rerunning a stage, and the cache of fits

Rerunning a stage removes its folder and every later stage's. Fitted models
live outside the stages, in `fits/response/`, because the three testing
stages share them: clearing a testing stage keeps them, and clearing QC
removes them.

Each part file of the cache says inside itself how its fits were made, in the
Parquet file's own metadata. A reader takes fits only from a part made as it
would make them, and ignores any other part.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## R

```{r}
folder <- file.path(out, "analysis-r")
str(fit_parts(folder)[[1]]$identity)
fmt_clear_stage(folder, "calibration")
cat("after clearing calibration:", fmt_stages_run(folder), "| parts of fits kept:", length(fit_parts(folder)), "\n")
fmt_clear_stage(folder, "qc")
cat("after clearing qc:         ", fmt_stages_run(folder), "| parts of fits kept:", length(fit_parts(folder)), "\n")
```

A part made with another fitting method is allowed and unused:

```{r}
other <- "conformance/valid/analyses/fits_made_with_another_method"
c(parts = length(fit_parts(other)), fits_a_reader_takes = NROW(fmt_read_analysis(other)$tables[[FITS]]),
  problems_reported = nrow(validate_analysis(other, "conformance/valid/highmoi_written_by_r.h5mu")))
```

## Python

```{python}
folder = out / "analysis-python"
print(json.dumps(sf.fit_parts(folder)[0][1], indent=1))
sf.clear_stage(folder, "calibration")
print("after clearing calibration:", sf.stages_run(folder), "| parts of fits kept:", len(sf.fit_parts(folder)))
sf.clear_stage(folder, "qc")
print("after clearing qc:         ", sf.stages_run(folder), "| parts of fits kept:", len(sf.fit_parts(folder)))
```

A part made with another fitting method is allowed and unused:

```{python}
other = "conformance/valid/analyses/fits_made_with_another_method"
{"parts": len(sf.fit_parts(other)), "fits_a_reader_takes": len(sf.read_analysis(other)["tables"].get(sf.FITS, [])),
 "problems_reported": len(sf.validate_analysis(other, "conformance/valid/highmoi_written_by_r.h5mu"))}
```

:::

## What this notebook does not show

- **Whether the files hold everything an analysis needs.** Only rebuilding a
  real sceptre object tests that. A suite that did so was removed for now; see
  `README.md`.
- **Anything about results**: whether sceptre and pysceptre compute the same
  p-values from these files is a question about the packages.
- **Scale.** These examples have 500 and 1,000 cells. One run on 207,324 cells
  is reported in `RATIONALE.md`, Appendix A.
